sanskrit: pravartamāne saṃgrāme tasminn atibhayaṃkare droṇasya miṣato vyūhaṃ bhittvā prāviśad ārjuniḥ
english: As that most terrifying battle raged on, the son of Arjuna, before Droṇa's very eyes, broke through the formation and entered it.

sanskrit: taṃ praviṣṭaṃ parān ghnantaṃ śatrumadhye mahābalam hastyaśvarathapattyaughāḥ parivavrur udāyudhāḥ
english: As that mighty one entered and struck down the foe in the enemy's midst, throngs of elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers, weapons upraised, closed in around him.

sanskrit: nānāvāditraninadaiḥ kṣveḍitotkruṣṭagarjitaiḥ huṃkāraiḥ siṃhanādaiś ca tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti nisvanaiḥ
english: With the din of varied instruments, with whoops and shouts and roars, with snarls and lion-cries and cries of "Stand! Stand!",

sanskrit: ghorair halahalāśabdair mā gās tiṣṭhaihi mām iti asāv aham amutreti pravadanto muhur muhuḥ
english: with dreadful clamoring uproar—"Do not flee! Stand! Come to me! That one is mine, I am here!"—crying out again and again,

sanskrit: bṛṃhitaiḥ śiñjitair hāsaiḥ khuranemisvanair api saṃnādayanto vasudhām abhidudruvur ārjunim
english: with the trumpeting of elephants, the jingling of ornaments, with laughter, and the clatter of hooves and wheel-rims, making the earth resound, they rushed upon the son of Arjuna.

sanskrit: teṣām āpatatāṃ vīraḥ pūrvaṃ śīghram atho dṛḍham kṣiprāstro nyavadhīd vrātān marmajño marmabhedibhiḥ
english: As they fell upon him, the hero—swift of weapon and knowing the vital points—slew their bands first quickly, then surely, with shafts that pierced the vitals.

sanskrit: te hanyamānāś ca tathā nānāliṅgaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ abhipetus tam evājau śalabhā iva pāvakam
english: Though they were thus being slain by his sharp arrows of many kinds, they hurled themselves upon him in the fray like moths into a flame.

sanskrit: tatas teṣāṃ śarīraiś ca śarīrāvayavaiś ca saḥ saṃtastāra kṣitiṃ kṣipraṃ kuśair vedim ivādhvare
english: Then with their bodies and the limbs of their bodies he swiftly strewed the ground, as one strews the altar with kuśa grass at a sacrifice.

sanskrit: baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇān saśarāvarakārmukān sāsicarmāṅkuśābhīśūn satomaraparaśvadhān
english: Their arms bound with iguana-hide and finger-guards, bearing arrows, shields, and bows, with swords, leather, goads, and reins, with lances and battle-axes,

sanskrit: saguḍāyomukhaprāsān sarṣṭitomarapaṭṭiśān sabhiṇḍipālaparighān saśaktivarakampanān
english: with iron-tipped barbed javelins, with spears, lances, and tridents, with slings and clubs, with darts and excellent quivering pikes,

sanskrit: sapratodamahāśaṅkhān sakuntān sakacagrahān samudgarakṣepaṇīyān sapāśaparighopalān
english: with goads and great conches, with barbed spears, with grappling-hooks, with mallets and slingstones, with nooses, bludgeons, and stones—

sanskrit: sakeyūrāṅgadān bāhūn hṛdyagandhānulepanān saṃcicchedārjunir vṛttāṃs tvadīyānāṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: the rounded arms of your men, adorned with armlets and bracelets and anointed with fragrant unguents, the son of Arjuna severed by the thousand.

sanskrit: taiḥ sphuradbhir mahārāja śuśubhe lohitokṣitaiḥ pañcāsyaiḥ pannagaiś chinnair garuḍeneva māriṣa
english: With those quivering, blood-drenched arms, O great king, the field shone as if with five-headed serpents cut asunder by Garuḍa, good sir.

sanskrit: sunāsānanakeśāntair avraṇaiś cārukuṇḍalaiḥ saṃdaṣṭauṣṭhapuṭaiḥ krodhāt kṣaradbhiḥ śoṇitaṃ bahu
english: With heads of fair noses, faces, and flowing hair, unblemished, with lovely earrings, with lips bitten in rage, streaming much blood,

sanskrit: cārusraṅmukuṭoṣṇīṣair maṇiratnavirājitaiḥ vinālanalinākārair divākaraśaśiprabhaiḥ
english: with lovely garlands, crowns, and diadems, gleaming with gems and jewels, shaped like stalkless lotuses, with the radiance of sun and moon,

sanskrit: hitapriyaṃvadaiḥ kāle bahubhiḥ puṇyagandhibhiḥ dviṣacchirobhiḥ pṛthivīm avatastāra phālguṇiḥ
english: with many sweet-spoken heads of the foe, which had spoken kindly and well in their time and were of holy fragrance, the son of Phalguna covered the earth.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākārān vidhivat kalpitān rathān vīṣāmukhān vitriveṇūn vyastadaṇḍakabandhurān
english: Chariots shaped like the cities of the gandharvas, fashioned according to rule—their shafts shattered, their triple-poles broken, their staves and yokes scattered,

sanskrit: vijaṅghakūbarākṣāṃś ca vinemīn anarān api vicakropaskaropasthān bhagnopakaraṇān api
english: their axles, poles, and pins gone, their rims gone, their drivers gone, their wheels, gear, and seats undone, their fittings broken as well,

sanskrit: praśātitopakaraṇān hatayodhān sahasraśaḥ śarair viśakalīkurvan dikṣu sarvāsv adṛśyata
english: their equipment hewn away, their warriors slain by the thousand—shattering them to fragments with his arrows, he was seen in every direction.

sanskrit: punar dvipān dvipārohān vaijayantyaṅkuśadhvajān tūṇān varmāṇy atho kakṣyā graiveyān atha kambalān
english: And again the elephants and their riders, the banners, goads, and standards, the quivers, the armor, the girths, the neck-ropes, the blankets,

sanskrit: ghaṇṭāḥ śuṇḍān viṣāṇāgrān kṣurapālān padānugān śarair niśitadhārāgraiḥ śātravāṇām aśātayat
english: the bells, the trunks, the tusk-tips, the foot-guards, and the attendants of the enemy—all these he cut down with his keen-edged, sharp-pointed arrows.

sanskrit: vanāyujān pārvatīyān kāmbojāraṭṭabāhlikān sthiravāladhikarṇākṣāñ javanān sādhuvāhinaḥ
english: Steeds from Vanāyu, from the mountains, from Kāmboja, Āraṭṭa, and Bāhlika—of steady tails, ears, and eyes, swift and well-trained to bear,

sanskrit: svārūḍhāñ śikṣitair yodhaiḥ śaktyṛṣṭiprāsayodhibhiḥ vidhvastacāmarakuthān viprakīrṇaprakīrṇakān
english: well-mounted by trained warriors who fought with darts, lances, and javelins—their chowries and trappings undone, their plumes scattered about,

sanskrit: nirastajihvānayanān niṣkīrṇāntrayakṛdghanān hatārohān bhinnabhāṇḍān kravyādagaṇamodanān
english: with tongues and eyes thrust out, with entrails, livers, and hearts spilling forth, their riders slain, their harness broken, a feast for the flesh-eating throngs,

sanskrit: nikṛttavarmakavacāñ śakṛnmūtrāsṛgāplutān nipātayann aśvavarāṃs tāvakān so 'bhyarocata
english: their armor and mail cut away, drenched in dung and urine and blood—felling these fine horses of your men, he shone resplendent.

sanskrit: eko viṣṇur ivācintyaḥ kṛtvā prāk karma duṣkaram tathā vimathitaṃ tena tryaṅgaṃ tava balaṃ mahat vyahanat sa padātyoghāṃs tvadīyān eva bhārata
english: Alone, unfathomable as Viṣṇu, having wrought before this a deed hard to do, he so churned up the three branches of your great host; and he struck down the floods of your foot-soldiers as well, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: evam ekena tāṃ senāṃ saubhadreṇa śitaiḥ śaraiḥ bhṛśaṃ viprahatāṃ dṛṣṭvā skandenevāsurīṃ camūm
english: Seeing that army thus grievously battered by Subhadrā's son alone with his sharp arrows, as the asuras' host was once smitten by Skanda,

sanskrit: tvadīyās tava putrāś ca vīkṣamāṇā diśo daśa saṃśuṣkāsyāś calannetrāḥ prasvinnā lomaharṣaṇāḥ
english: your men and your sons, gazing about them in all ten directions, their mouths gone dry, their eyes darting, sweating, their hair on end,

sanskrit: palāyanakṛtotsāhā nirutsāhā dviṣajjaye gotranāmabhir anyonyaṃ krandanto jīvitaiṣiṇaḥ
english: bent on fleeing, drained of all heart for the conquest of the foe, calling out to one another by clan and name, longing for their lives,

sanskrit: hatān putrāṃs tathā pitṝn suhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavān prātiṣṭhanta samutsṛjya tvarayanto hayadvipān
english: abandoning their slain sons and fathers, their friends, kinsmen, and relations, they took flight, urging on their horses and elephants.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tāṃ prabhagnāṃ camūṃ dṛṣṭvā saubhadreṇāmitaujasā duryodhano bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ svayaṃ saubhadram abhyayāt
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing that host shattered by the son of Subhadrā of boundless might, Duryodhana, sorely enraged, advanced himself against the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: tato rājānam āvṛttaṃ saubhadraṃ prati saṃyuge dṛṣṭvā droṇo 'bravīd yodhān paryāpnuta narādhipam
english: Then, seeing the king turn toward Subhadrā's son in the fray, Droṇa said to the warriors, "Shield the lord of men!

sanskrit: purābhimanyur lakṣyaṃ naḥ paśyatāṃ hanti vīryavān tam ādravata mā bhaiṣṭa kṣipraṃ rakṣata kauravam
english: Before mighty Abhimanyu slays the mark of our gaze—rush upon him! Do not fear! Swiftly guard the Kaurava!"

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtajñā balinaḥ suhṛdo jitakāśinaḥ trāsyamānā bhayād vīraṃ parivavrus tavātmajam
english: Then those grateful, mighty comrades, flushed with victory yet harried by fear, surrounded your son to shield him from the hero.

sanskrit: droṇo drauṇiḥ kṛpaḥ karṇaḥ kṛtavarmā ca saubalaḥ bṛhadbalo madrarājo bhūrir bhūriśravāḥ śalaḥ
english: Droṇa, the son of Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, Kṛtavarman, and the son of Subala, Bṛhadbala, the king of the Madras, Bhūri, Bhūriśravas, and Śala,

sanskrit: pauravo vṛṣasenaś ca visṛjantaḥ śitāñ śarān saubhadraṃ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā samavākiran
english: the Paurava and Vṛṣasena—loosing sharp arrows, they overwhelmed the son of Subhadrā with a great rain of shafts.

sanskrit: saṃmohayitvā tam atha duryodhanam amocayan āsyād grāsam ivākṣiptaṃ mamṛṣe nārjunātmajaḥ
english: Having bewildered him, they then bore Duryodhana off to safety; but the son of Arjuna could not brook it, as a lion cannot brook a morsel snatched from its jaws.

sanskrit: tāñ śaraugheṇa mahatā sāśvasūtān mahārathān vimukhīkṛtya saubhadraḥ siṃhanādam athānadat
english: With a great flood of arrows the son of Subhadrā turned those great chariot-warriors back, horses and drivers and all, and then let loose a lion's roar.

sanskrit: tasya nādaṃ tataḥ śrutvā siṃhasyevāmiṣaiṣiṇaḥ nāmṛṣyanta susaṃrabdhāḥ punar droṇamukhā rathāḥ
english: Hearing his cry, like that of a lion craving its prey, the chariot-warriors led by Droṇa, greatly incensed, could not endure it once again.

sanskrit: ta enaṃ koṣṭhakīkṛtya rathavaṃśena māriṣa vyasṛjann iṣujālāni nānāliṅgāni saṃghaśaḥ
english: Penning him in with their array of chariots, good sir, they loosed nets of arrows of many kinds upon him in massed volleys.

sanskrit: tāny antarikṣe ciccheda pautras tava śitaiḥ śaraiḥ tāṃś caiva prativivyādha tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Your grandson cut these apart in mid-air with his sharp arrows, and pierced those warriors in return—and that was a marvel to behold.

sanskrit: tatas te kopitās tena śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ parivavrur jighāṃsantaḥ saubhadram apalāyinam
english: Then, provoked by him with arrows like venomous serpents, they surrounded the unflinching son of Subhadrā, bent on his death.

sanskrit: samudram iva paryastaṃ tvadīyaṃ tad balārṇavam abhimanyur dadhāraiko veleva makarālayam
english: That ocean-host of yours, surging like the sea, Abhimanyu alone held back, as the shore holds back the abode of sea-monsters.

sanskrit: śūrāṇāṃ yudhyamānānāṃ nighnatām itaretaram abhimanyoḥ pareṣāṃ ca nāsīt kaś cit parāṅmukhaḥ
english: Among the heroes fighting and striking one another—Abhimanyu and the foe alike—not one turned his face away.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu ghore saṃgrāme vartamāne bhayaṃkare duḥsaho navabhir bāṇair abhimanyum avidhyata
english: While that dreadful, terrifying battle raged on, Duḥsaha pierced Abhimanyu with nine arrows.

sanskrit: duḥśāsano dvādaśabhiḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tribhiḥ droṇas tu saptadaśabhiḥ śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ
english: Duḥśāsana struck him with twelve, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat with three, and Droṇa with seventeen arrows like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: viviṃśatis tu viṃśatyā kṛtavarmā ca saptabhiḥ bṛhadbalas tathāṣṭābhir aśvatthāmā ca saptabhiḥ
english: Viviṃśati with twenty, Kṛtavarman with seven, Bṛhadbala likewise with eight, and Aśvatthāman with seven,

sanskrit: bhūriśravās tribhir bāṇair madreśaḥ ṣaḍbhir āśugaiḥ dvābhyāṃ śarābhyāṃ śakunis tribhir duryodhano nṛpaḥ
english: Bhūriśravas with three arrows, the lord of the Madras with six swift shafts, Śakuni with two, and king Duryodhana with three.

sanskrit: sa tu tān prativivyādha tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ nṛtyann iva mahārāja cāpahastaḥ pratāpavān
english: But he pierced each of them in return with three straight-flying shafts, as if dancing, O great king, bow in hand, that splendid warrior.

sanskrit: tato 'bhimanyuḥ saṃkruddhas tāpyamānas tavātmajaiḥ vidarśayan vai sumahac chikṣaurasakṛtaṃ balam
english: Then Abhimanyu, enraged and sorely pressed by your sons, displayed the mighty power of his training and his own native strength.

sanskrit: garuḍānilaraṃhobhir yantur vākyakarair hayaiḥ dāntair aśmakadāyādaṃ tvaramāṇo 'bhyahārayat vivyādha cainaṃ daśabhir bāṇais tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: With horses swift as Garuḍa or the wind, tamed and obedient to their driver's word, he hastened to attack the heir of Aśmaka, pierced him with ten arrows, and cried, "Stand!"

sanskrit: tasyābhimanyur daśabhir bāṇaiḥ sūtaṃ hayān dhvajam bāhū dhanuḥ śiraś corvyāṃ smayamāno 'bhyapātayat
english: With ten arrows Abhimanyu, smiling, brought down to earth his driver, his horses, his banner, his arms, his bow, and his head.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin hate vīre saubhadreṇāśmakeśvare saṃcacāla balaṃ sarvaṃ palāyanaparāyaṇam
english: Then, when that hero, the lord of Aśmaka, was slain by the son of Subhadrā, the whole host wavered and gave itself over to flight.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaḥ kṛpo droṇo drauṇir gāndhārarāṭ śalaḥ śalyo bhūriśravāḥ krāthaḥ somadatto viviṃśatiḥ
english: Then Karṇa, Kṛpa, Droṇa, the son of Droṇa, the king of Gāndhāra, Śala, Śalya, Bhūriśravas, Krātha, Somadatta, Viviṃśati,

sanskrit: vṛṣasenaḥ suṣeṇaś ca kuṇḍabhedī pratardanaḥ vṛndārako lalitthaś ca prabāhur dīrghalocanaḥ duryodhanaś ca saṃkruddhaḥ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Vṛṣasena and Suṣeṇa, Kuṇḍabhedin, Pratardana, Vṛndāraka, Lalittha, Prabāhu, Dīrghalocana, and Duryodhana, all in fury, overwhelmed him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: so 'tikruddho maheṣvāsair abhimanyur ajihmagaiḥ śaram ādatta karṇāya parakāyāvabhedanam
english: Greatly enraged by those mighty archers, Abhimanyu took up against Karṇa a straight-flying arrow that pierces the bodies of foes.

sanskrit: tasya bhittvā tanutrāṇaṃ dehaṃ nirbhidya cāśugaḥ prāviśad dharaṇīṃ rājan valmīkam iva pannagaḥ
english: That swift shaft, cleaving his armor and piercing his body, entered the earth, O king, like a serpent entering an anthill.

sanskrit: sa tenātiprahāreṇa vyathito vihvalann iva saṃcacāla raṇe karṇaḥ kṣitikampe yathācalaḥ
english: Stricken by that mighty blow and reeling as if dazed, Karṇa swayed upon the field like a mountain in an earthquake.

sanskrit: athānyair niśitair bāṇaiḥ suṣeṇaṃ dīrghalocanam kuṇḍabhediṃ ca saṃkruddhas tribhis trīn avadhīd balī
english: Then with other keen arrows the mighty one, in his wrath, slew the three—Suṣeṇa, Dīrghalocana, and Kuṇḍabhedin—with three shafts.

sanskrit: karṇas taṃ pañcaviṃśatyā nārācānāṃ samarpayat aśvatthāmā ca viṃśatyā kṛtavarmā ca saptabhiḥ
english: Karṇa let fly at him twenty-five iron shafts, Aśvatthāman twenty, and Kṛtavarman seven.

sanskrit: sa śarārditasarvāṅgaḥ kruddhaḥ śakrātmajātmajaḥ vicaran dṛśyate sainye pāśahasta ivāntakaḥ
english: His every limb tormented by arrows, the son of Indra's son, in his wrath, was seen ranging through the host like Death with noose in hand.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ ca bāṇavarṣeṇa samīpastham avākirat udakrośan mahābāhus tava sainyāni bhīṣayan
english: And with a rain of arrows he overwhelmed Śalya, who stood close by, that mighty-armed one crying aloud and striking terror into your armies.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa viddho 'stravidā marmabhidbhir ajihmagaiḥ śalyo rājan rathopasthe niṣasāda mumoha ca
english: Then, pierced by that master of weapons with straight shafts that cleave the vitals, Śalya, O king, sank down upon the floor of his chariot and swooned away.

sanskrit: taṃ hi viddhaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā saubhadreṇa yaśasvinā saṃprādravac camūḥ sarvā bhāradvājasya paśyataḥ
english: Seeing him so pierced by the glorious son of Subhadrā, the whole host took to flight before the very eyes of the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: prekṣantas taṃ mahābāhuṃ rukmapuṅkhaiḥ samāvṛtam tvadīyāś ca palāyante mṛgāḥ siṃhārditā iva
english: Beholding that mighty-armed one encompassed by his gold-feathered arrows, your men too fled, like deer harried by a lion.

sanskrit: sa tu raṇayaśasābhipūjyamānaḥ; pitṛsuracāraṇasiddhayakṣasaṃghaiḥ avanitalagataiś ca bhūtasaṃghair; ativibabhau hutabhug yathājyasiktaḥ
english: And he, honored for his glory in battle by the throngs of ancestors, gods, cāraṇas, siddhas, and yakṣas, and by the hosts of beings upon the earth, blazed forth like fire fed with clarified butter.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tathā pramathamānaṃ taṃ maheṣvāsam ajihmagaiḥ ārjuniṃ māmakāḥ sarve ke tv enaṃ samavākiran
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: As that mighty archer, the son of Arjuna, churned them so with his straight shafts, which of my men all overwhelmed him?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājan kumārasya raṇe vikrīḍitaṃ mahat bibhitsato rathānīkaṃ bhāradvājena rakṣitam
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king, the great sport of the youth in battle, as he sought to break through the chariot-array guarded by the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: madreśaṃ sāditaṃ dṛṣṭvā saubhādreṇāśugai raṇe śalyād avarajaḥ kruddhaḥ kiran bāṇān samabhyayāt
english: Seeing the lord of the Madras struck down by the son of Subhadrā with swift shafts in the fray, Śalya's younger brother, enraged, advanced upon him, scattering arrows.

sanskrit: sa viddhvā daśabhir bāṇaiḥ sāśvayantāram ārjunim udakrośan mahāśabdaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Piercing the son of Arjuna, horses and driver and all, with ten arrows, he cried out in a great voice, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: tasyārjuniḥ śirogrīvaṃ pāṇipādaṃ dhanur hayān chatraṃ dhvajaṃ niyantāraṃ triveṇuṃ śamyupaskaram
english: His head and neck, hands and feet, his bow, his horses, his parasol, his banner, his driver, the triple-pole, the pegs and gear,

sanskrit: cakre yugeṣāṃ tūṇīrān anukarṣaṃ ca sāyakaiḥ patākāṃ cakragoptārau sarvopakaraṇāni ca vyadhamal lāghavāt tac ca dadṛśe nāsya kaś cana
english: the wheels, the yoke-shaft, the quivers, and the under-pole—with his arrows, and the pennon, the two wheel-guards, and all the fittings, the son of Arjuna shattered with such swiftness that none could mark how he did it.

sanskrit: sa papāta kṣitau kṣīṇaḥ praviddhābharaṇāmbaraḥ vāyuneva mahācaityaḥ saṃbhagno 'mitatejasā anugāś cāsya vitrastāḥ prādravan sarvatodiśam
english: He fell to the earth undone, his ornaments and garments scattered, like a great sacred tree snapped by the wind—broken by that one of boundless splendor; and his followers, terror-struck, fled in every direction.

sanskrit: ārjuneḥ karma tad dṛṣṭva praṇeduś ca samantataḥ nādena sarvabhūtāni sādhu sādhv iti bhārata
english: Seeing that deed of the son of Arjuna, all beings on every side cried out with a great shout, "Well done! Well done!", O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: śalyabhrātary athārugṇe bahuśas tasya sainikāḥ kulādhivāsanāmāni śrāvayanto 'rjunātmajam
english: Now that Śalya's brother was struck down, his soldiers in great numbers, proclaiming aloud to the son of Arjuna the names of their clans and dwelling-places,

sanskrit: abhyavartanta saṃkruddhā vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ rathair aśvair gajaiś cānye pādātaiś ca balotkaṭāḥ
english: advanced in fury, weapons of every kind in hand, some with chariots, horses, and elephants, others on foot, swollen with strength.

sanskrit: bāṇaśabdena mahatā khuranemisvanena ca huṃkāraiḥ kṣveḍitotkruṣṭaiḥ siṃhanādaiḥ sagarjitaiḥ
english: With the great twang of bowstrings and the clatter of hooves and wheel-rims, with snarls, whoops, and shouts, with lion-roars and bellowings,

sanskrit: jyātalatrasvanair anye garjanto 'rjunanandanam bruvantaś ca na no jīvan mokṣyase jīvatām iti
english: others with the twang of bowstring and finger-guard, roaring at the son of Arjuna and crying, "You shall not escape us alive while we yet live!"

sanskrit: tāṃs tathā bruvato dṛṣṭvā saubhadraḥ prahasann iva yo yaḥ sma prāharat pūrvaṃ taṃ taṃ vivyādha patribhiḥ
english: Seeing them speak thus, the son of Subhadrā, as if smiling, pierced with his feathered shafts each man, one after another, who had first struck at him.

sanskrit: saṃdarśayiṣyann astrāṇi citrāṇi ca laghūni ca ārjuniḥ samare śūro mṛdupūrvam ayudhyata
english: Meaning to display his weapons, both wondrous and swift, the heroic son of Arjuna fought on in the battle, gently at first.
